svg.title: Auditing chinit for Azure: Four Portability Findings Between AWS and Azure
svg.desc: A provider interface is only ten percent of cloud portability. Auditing chinit on Azure uncovered four AWS-shaped assumptions in the shared boot pipeline: S3 endpoint env gates, static IP fallbacks, mismatched bundle checksums, and missing capability probes.

g.text: The Cloud-Neutral Bootstrapper Audit: AWS Assumptions vs. Portable Contracts
A provider factory is 10% of portability — the other 90% is removing one cloud's resource model from shared steps
WHAT BROKE ON AZURE (HIDDEN AWS ASSUMPTIONS)
THE PORTABLE CONTRACT IN CHINIT
1. "Neutral" Step with an AWS-Shaped Heart
configure_server_env treated empty s3_data_bucket as Fatal.
Azure Blob disks inline account/key in storage.xml — no env needed.
Result: Every Azure boot died at Step 7c
Provider-Scoped Step Contract
Gate CH_S3_ENDPOINT requirement explicitly on provider == aws;
on Azure, empty s3_data_bucket is valid and writes no env file.
Optional fields mean "not applicable here," not "broken"
2. Dynamic VMSS IPs Broke Static Identity Fallback
AWS could fall back to a static IP-octet map when lease fields
were omitted; Azure VMSS hands out dynamic IPs on every scale-out.
Result: Identity fell back to ephemeral platform hostnames
First-Class Lease Identity + Self-Healing Renewal
Render claim table & ceilings into every role spec; if a lease
expires during a transient PartitionKeyblip, lease-renew re-acquires
its own ordinal in place instead of leaving the node unclaimed
3. A Checksum Gate with Two Different Formulas
Terraform hashed a JSON map of bundle files; Azure's fetcher
hashed raw concatenated bytes and added a role-specific file.
Result: SHA256 digest could never match on Azure
Single Canonical Bundle Digest Across Clouds
Both clouds compute the exact same sorted key-digest structure
over the shared config bundle; verified by cross-cloud unit tests.
A validation gate is only real when both signers run the same math
4. 18-Release Pin Drift & Missing Remedy Probes
Azure image stayed pinned at v0.2.0 while AWS reached v0.2.18;
lease-lister & volume-grower capabilities were untested on Azure.
Full Capability Conformance Suite
Conformance suite exercises Claims + Lister + DNS + Volume Grower;
unsupported remedies fail loudly with named errors instead of silence.
Portability Rule: An unbooted second cloud will rot at its initial version pin — test the shared pipeline against both specs in CI
